text:
raj_runtime: Quick sync — proposing a short "prober" run to validate FlashAttn v2/v3 integration plans. Focus: kernel chooser correctness, batching heuristics under mixed seq distributions, and KV cache behavior when switching kernels. Canary target: dedicated-staging pools only.

olivia_perf: Sounds good. High-level from profiling: v3 wins on short/medium (<=512) — ~+8-12% tokens/sec. But we saw a regression for very long context (>2048) when KV warmup is poor: ~-6 to -9%. Need to reproduce with realistic prefix reuse.

maria_eng: Agree. My plan: run the prober with three workload mixes (chatty short, doc-heavy long, and mixed real-traffic replay). Each mix will exercise: kernel chooser latency, batch formation latency, and KV hit ratio. I added a small feature-flag matrix for the runs.

raj_runtime: Paste of the flag matrix I'm proposing:
```
# prober config (yaml-ish)
feature_flag: attn_chooser_prober
runs:
  - name: canary-v2-default
    kernel_pref: v2
    enable_v3: false
  - name: canary-auto-chooser
    kernel_pref: auto
    chooser_mode: latency_weighted
  - name: canary-force-v3
    kernel_pref: v3
    enable_v3: true
traffic_profiles: [short, long, mixed-replay]
metrics: [p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, kv_hit_rate, oom_count]
```

olivia_perf: For measurements, please ensure we capture per-token CPU/GPU utilization and kernel selection traces. Small script I used: `python tools/trace_kernel_choice.py --out=prober-traces.json`. That helps link a perf blip to a kernel swap.

jen_sre: Quick ops note: dedicated-staging has two pools (gpu-a, gpu-b). I'll schedule windows to avoid noisy neighbors. Canary window: 30m per run, with rollback on p95 > baseline + 15% or any new OOMs.

maria_eng: Also include a KV warmup variant: cold-start vs prewarmed caches. We saw different chooser behavior when KV misses spike. Added a step to replay 1h of prior traffic to warm caches before the main run.

raj_runtime: Acceptance criteria:
- no increase in OOMs
- p95 latency within +10% of current baseline for short workloads
- tokens/sec improvement >=4% for mixed profile OR consistent kernel fallback logic documented
- KV hit-rate not decreased by >3% for mixed profile

olivia_perf: One more: add a micro-benchmark for fused-attn kernel invocation overhead (small batch, many short sequences). v3 sometimes adds overhead for tiny batches.

maria_eng: Test harness changes I'll push: a new prober job in infra/ci named `attn_integration_prober`, job will accept the flag matrix and output csvs + trace json. I'll also include an auto-summary script that emits a short verdict: pass/fail + top 3 regressions.

raj_runtime: Rolling checklist for the run (short bullets):
- [ ] add prober job and configs (maria)
- [ ] schedule windows in staging (jen)
- [ ] deploy chooser telemetry with sampling (olivia)
- [ ] run short/long/mixed profiles (maria)
- [ ] collect traces & run auto-summary (maria/olivia)
- [ ] decide canary progression to dedicated-prod (team)

jen_sre: I'll create the calendar blocks and add the oncall rotation for the windows. Tagging incident responders as FYI.

ci-bot: prober-job template pushed: https://git.internal/repo/infra/attn_integration_prober/commit/8a3f2d

olivia_perf: Minor note: when reporting, include a small snippet linking kernel chooser decisions to sequence length distribution, e.g. `chooser picked v3 for ~78% of seq<=256, v2 for 62% of seq>2048` — that helps product teams understand tradeoffs.

maria_eng: I'll run a quick smoke tonight (staging) with a 10m warmup and post results here. If anyone wants to join the live run, ping me.

raj_runtime: Thanks all — let's keep this tight. If the prober shows consistent regression we will revert the chooser to a conservative policy by default and iterate. :thumbsup:
